'''Altay''' ([[Turkish language|Turkish]] for ''Red foal/colt'') is a Turkish [[List of main battle tanks by generation|fourth generation]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nationalinterest.org/blog/reboot/meet-altay-how-turkey-building-fourth-generation-tank-189695|title=Meet the Altay: How Turkey is Building a Fourth Generation Tank|first=Mark|last=Episkopos|date=16 July 2021|website=The National Interest|access-date=11 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Turkish Main Battle Tank Altay is Finally Entering Service - Technology Org | date=31 August 2025 | url=https://www.technology.org/2025/08/31/turkish-main-battle-tank-altay-is-finally-entering-service/ }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Türkiye's Altay T1 Tank Enters Service: NATO's New Armored Power in the South | date=28 August 2025 | url=https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/altay-t1-main-battle-tank-delivery-turkey-nato/ }}</ref> [[main battle tank]] designed by [[Otokar]], based on the South Korean [[K2 Black Panther]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nationalinterest.org/blog/buzz/turkey-set-be-tank-powerhouse-altay-main-battle-tank-211329|title=Turkey is Set to be a Tank Powerhouse with Altay Main Battle Tank|first=Peter|last=Suciu|date=6 June 2024}}</ref>. It is produced by [[BMC (Turkey)|BMC]] with design assistance and [[technology transfer]]ring by [[Hyundai Rotem]].<ref name="Design assistance and transfer of Technology 1" /> It is named in honor of Army General [[Fahrettin Altay]] who commanded the 5th Cavalry Corps in the final stage of the [[Turkish War of Independence]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.radikal.com.tr/Radikal.aspx?aType=RadikalDetay&ArticleID=890989&CategoryID=80 |title=Milli tank 'altay' için yola çıkıldı – Ekonomi Haberleri |publisher=Radikal |date=2008-07-30 |access-date=2015-02-28}}</ref>

Altay is combined with [[Mechanical and Chemical Industry Corporation|MKE]] [[MKE 120 mm tank gun|made 55 calibre 120&nbsp;mm main gun]], [[Roketsan]] made advanced composite and [[reactive armor]] package along with [[Aselsan]] made electronics such as [[active protection system|active protection]], [[Remote controlled weapon station|remote controlled weapon]] and [[fire control system]]s. The first batch will be produced using [[HD Hyundai Infracore]] engine and [[SNT Dynamics]] transmission, while the second batch will use [[BMC (Turkey)|BMC]]-made domestic powerpack.<ref name="Korean Powerpack 1" />

Mass production officially began on 5 September 2025. It officially entered service on 28 October 2025.<ref>{{cite web | title=New-generation Altay tank enters Turkish army service | date=28 October 2025 | url=https://defence-blog.com/new-generation-altay-tank-enters-turkish-army-service/ }}</ref>

==History==
The National Tank Production Project (Turkish: ''MİTÜP – Milli Tank Üretimi Projesi'') was an initiative developed in the mid-1990s to establish independent and robust infrastructure for the production, development and maintenance of main battle tanks used by the [[Turkish Armed Forces]].<ref>[http://www.otokar.com.tr/en/media_relations/p_haber_detay.aspx?haber=147 Turkey's National Main Battle Tank Project (ALTAY) started with the ceremony held at Otokar factory] otokar.com.tr 1 August 2008 {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140408212341/http://www.otokar.com.tr/en/media_relations/p_haber_detay.aspx?haber=147|date=8 April 2014}}</ref><ref name="ssm">{{cite web|url=http://www.ssm.gov.tr/home/projects/land/BattleTanks/Sayfalar/ALTAYPROJECT.aspx |access-date=7 October 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722082812/http://www.ssm.gov.tr/home/projects/land/BattleTanks/Sayfalar/ALTAYPROJECT.aspx |title=ALTAY PROJECT; Undersecretariat for defence Industries |archive-date=22 July 2011 }}</ref> In order to improve the current technical capabilities of the Turkish defense industries and increase the amount of domestic contribution towards national defense, the Undersecreteriat for Defense Industries decided that a "National Tank" will serve as a catalyst for uniting certain Turkish defense companies around a common goal and for providing the Turkish military with extra firepower in the form of a modern tank. This is Turkey's first MBT development program since 1943, when prototypes of a Turkish national tank were produced in [[Kırıkkale]],<ref>{{cite web | title=Yarım kalan hayal gerçek oldu: İlk tankımızın 80 yıllık sırrı - Son Dakika Flaş Haberler | date=2 November 2025 | url=https://www.cnnturk.com/turkiye/yarim-kalan-hayal-gercek-oldu-ilk-tankimizin-80-yillik-sirri-2354838 }}</ref> but 1943's program never reached full-scale mass production. The Turkish Ministry of Defense allocated a budget of $1 billion for the development of the Altay.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ensonhaber.com/milli-helikopterimiz-parmak-isirtiyor-2013-01-28.html |title=Milli helikopterimiz parmak ısırtıyor |publisher=En son haber |date=2013-01-28 |access-date=2015-02-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130131004704/http://www.ensonhaber.com/milli-helikopterimiz-parmak-isirtiyor-2013-01-28.html |archive-date=31 January 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Development==
The project was initiated with an agreement signed between [[Otokar]] and the Undersecretariat for Defense Industries of the [[Republic of Turkey]] on 30 March 2007, when the Defense Industries Executive Committee awarded a contract worth approximately $500&nbsp;million to Otokar for the design, development and production of four prototypes of a national [[main battle tank]]. On July 29, 2008, Turkey and [[Hyundai Rotem]] signed a ₩500 billion (approximately US$540 million) design assistance and technology transfer contract for tank development. This contract consists of design assistance and technology transfer related to the development of systems, armor packages, and 120&nbsp;mm guns necessary for the development of Altay tanks, and includes design assistance and technology transfer of Hyundai Rotem, [[Hyundai WIA]], and [[Agency for Defense Development]] throughout the development process.<ref name="Design assistance and transfer of Technology 1" />

The first 3D image of the MBT was released to the public on 7 April 2010 during a press release by the Undersecreteriat for Defense Industries of the Republic of Turkey.<ref name="TRdefenceColombia">{{cite web |url=http://www.trdefence.com/?p=335 |title=Otokar unveils the Altay MBT |publisher=TR Defence |date=2010-04-07 |access-date=2015-02-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100413222340/http://trdefence.com/?p=335 |archive-date=13 April 2010 |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2012, Otokar General Manager Serdar Görgüç announced that the company was considering the development of an electric engine for the Altay.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/otokar-mulls-making-of-domestic-electric-tank.aspx?pageID=238&nID=18494&NewsCatID=345|title=Otokar mulls making of domestic 'electric tank'|date=15 April 2012 |publisher=Hurriyetdailynews.com|access-date=2015-02-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919220132/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/otokar-mulls-making-of-domestic-electric-tank.aspx?pageID=238&nID=18494&NewsCatID=345|archive-date=19 September 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> However, the electric engine is probably no longer under consideration. The military electronics company [[Aselsan]] manufactures and integrates the Volkan III modular fire control system, command, control and information systems, while state-owned MKEK (Mechanical and Chemical Industries Corporation) produce [[MKE 120 mm tank gun]]. Another state-owned company, [[Roketsan]], produces an indigenous armor. The first prototype Altay was ready for use by the end of 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sabah.com.tr/ekonomi/2012/11/13/milli-tank-altayin-uretim-seruveni|title=Milli Tank Altay'ın üretim serüveni|access-date=16 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150920065239/http://www.sabah.com.tr/ekonomi/2012/11/13/milli-tank-altayin-uretim-seruveni|archive-date=20 September 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Once the prototypes are produced and tested, the Undersecreteriat for Defense Industries of the Republic of Turkey will prepare and execute a separate order for the first lot of 250 tanks. A total of 1,000 MBTs are planned to be produced in four separate lots of 250 units. Every delivered lot is expected to have additional upgrades.<ref>{{cite web |title=ANKARA – Turkish main battle tank project aims to meet needs of Turkish Armed Forces (TSK) |url=http://www.turkishpress.com/news.asp?id=133903 |access-date=21 November 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070922071251/http://www.turkishpress.com/news.asp?id=133903 |archive-date=22 September 2007}}</ref> Otokar completed all infrastructure planning and programming for mass production. [[Koç Holding]] Vice Chair and Otokar Chair Ali Koç said mass production was expected to start 18–22 months after their offer was accepted.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/koc-awaits-govt-approval-to-start-mass-production-of-domestic-turkish-battle-tank-altay.aspx?pageID=238&nID=105954&NewsCatID=345 |title=Koç awaits gov't approval to start mass production of domestic Turkish battle tank Altay |publisher=hurriyetdaillynews.com |date=2016-11-10 |access-date=2016-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121232149/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/koc-awaits-govt-approval-to-start-mass-production-of-domestic-turkish-battle-tank-altay.aspx?pageID=238&nID=105954&NewsCatID=345 |archive-date=21 November 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref>
[[File:Scale model of Altay.jpg|thumb|Scale model of Altay T1]] 
However, on 9 November 2018, Turkish [[Presidency of Defense Industries]] signed an agreement with [[BMC (Turkey)|BMC]] for mass production of the tank.<ref name="SSB 1"/> In the process, BMC replaced Otokar as the main contractor and responsible for further developments.{{citation needed|date=November 2025}}

The production of Altay has been delayed since 2018, as the programme was relying on German 1,500&nbsp;hp [[MTU Friedrichshafen|MTU engines]] and RENK transmissions,<ref name="military-today">{{Cite web|url=http://www.military-today.com/tanks/altay.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120904011102/http://www.military-today.com/tanks/altay.htm|url-status=usurped|archive-date=4 September 2012|title=Altay - Prototype main battle tank}}</ref> because of the German federal arms embargo on Turkey due to their [[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War|involvement in the Syrian Civil War]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.defensenews.com/industry/2020/11/19/turkey-in-talks-with-south-korea-to-salvage-altay-tank-program/ |title=Turkey in talks with South Korea to salvage Altay tank program |website=Defense News |date=19 November 2020 }}</ref> Another request from [[Mitsubishi Heavy Industries]] was also declined.<ref>{{cite web | title=Japan Decides Against Turkish-Azerbaijan Tank Deal &#124; Eurasianet | url=https://eurasianet.org/japan-decides-against-turkish-azerbaijan-tank-deal }}</ref>

However, BMC Power, a subsidiary of BMC, replaced MTU as engine subcontractor for 1,500&nbsp;hp engine. BMC Power is the designer and manufacturer of the serial production [[BATU V12]] 1,500&nbsp;hp engine.<ref name="V12 Project - developed from scratch by BMC POWER">{{cite web | url=https://www.bmcpower.com.tr/en/page/29/batu-projesi | title=BMC Power }}</ref><ref name="V12 Project">{{cite web |url= https://www.bmcpower.com.tr/en/page/29/batu-projesi| title = V12 Project |publisher= BMC Power |access-date= 11 August 2021}}</ref><ref name="Turkey Reports Successful Test of ‘Homegrown’ Tank Engine">{{cite web| url=https://www.thedefensepost.com/2021/05/07/turkey-tests-homegrown-tank-engine/| title=Turkey Reports Successful Test of 'Homegrown' Tank Engine| date=7 May 2021}}</ref>

On 10 March 2021, BMC announced that it plans to import a Korean power pack that combines [[Doosan|Doosan Infracore]] (now [[HD Hyundai Infracore]]) [[DV27K]] engine and [[SNT Dynamics]] [[EST15K]] transmission and complete the performance test of the Altay tank according to Turkey's own standards as soon as possible.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news1.kr/articles/?4235459|title=터키 차세대 전차 '알타이'에 '국산파워팩' 수출|publisher=News1 Korea|date=10 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210316123242/https://www.news1.kr/articles/?4235459|archive-date=16 March 2021|access-date=16 March 2021|author=Kim Min-seok}}</ref>

On 11 August 2021, the [[South Korea]]n [[Defense Acquisition Program Administration]] announced that it was looking for a Korean company to develop an improved SNT Dynamics EST15K transmission for use in Altay and [[K2 Black Panther]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dtaq.re.kr/ko/notice/notice.jsp?mode=view&article_no=154804&board_wrapper=/ko/notice/notice.jsp&pager.offset=0&board_no=25|title=2021년 2차 무기체계 개조개발 지원사업 지원과제 및 주관기업 모집 공고|publisher=Defense Agency for Technology and Quality|date=11 August 2021|archive-url=https://archive.today/20211025085843/https://www.dtaq.re.kr/ko/notice/notice.jsp?mode=view&article_no=154804&board_wrapper=/ko/notice/notice.jsp&pager.offset=0&board_no=25|archive-date=25 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021|author=[[Defense Acquisition Program Administration]]}}</ref>

On 7 October 2021, the South Korean Defense Acquisition Program Administration announced that it is looking for a Korean company to develop an indigenous [[Transmission control unit]] to replace the German Transmission control unit used in the SNT Dynamics EST15K transmission to export transmissions to Turkey.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dtaq.re.kr/ko/notice/notice.jsp?mode=view&article_no=155168&board_no=25|title=「K2 전차 변속제어기 (TCU) 변속제어 소프트웨어 부품성능개량개발」 일반부품 국산화사업 주관기업 모집공고|publisher=Defense Agency for Technology and Quality|date=7 October 2021|archive-url=https://archive.today/20211025100033/https://www.dtaq.re.kr/ko/notice/notice.jsp?mode=view&article_no=155168&board_no=25|archive-date=25 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021|author=[[Defense Acquisition Program Administration]]}}</ref>

On 22 October 2021, Kang Eun-ho, head of South Korea's Defense Acquisition Program Administration, said he had approved the export of Hyundai Doosan Infracore DV27K engines and SNT Dynamics EST15K transmissions to Turkey during a meeting with Turkish Foreign Minister [[Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu]] visiting South Korea.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20211022165300108|title=터키 전차에 국산 파워팩 탑재…터키 외무 "수출 승인받아"|publisher=[[Yonhap News Agency]]|date=22 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211025101338/https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20211022165300108|archive-date=25 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021|author=Kim Seung-uk |work=연합뉴스 }}</ref>

At the Antalya Diplomacy Forum held on March 11, 2022, Ismail Demir, president of Turkish Defense Industries (SSB), revealed that he was testing Hyundai Doosan Infracore DV27K engine and SNT Dynamics EST15K transmission imported from South Korea and he said in May that he will be able to see a prototype of Altay that combines Korean engines and transmissions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.turkishdefencenews.com/south-korean-engine-to-power-turkeys-altay-tank/|title=South Korean Engine to Power Turkey's ALTAY Tank|publisher=Turkish Defence News|date=16 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220315233206/https://www.turkishdefencenews.com/south-korean-engine-to-power-turkeys-altay-tank/|archive-date=15 March 2022|access-date=15 March 2022|author=Kamer KURUNÇ}}</ref>

In August 2022, the durability test of the powerpack combined with the DV27K engine and EST15K transmission imported from South Korea is underway, and if the durability test succeeds, the first 250 Altay will be produced by integrating the Korean powerpack.<ref name="Defenceturk 220811">{{cite web|url=https://www.defenceturk.net/altay-tanki-2025de-milli-guc-grubuna-sahip-olacak|title=ALTAY tankı 2025'de milli güç grubuna sahip olacak|publisher=Defenceturk|date=11 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220901195406/https://www.defenceturk.net/altay-tanki-2025de-milli-guc-grubuna-sahip-olacak|archive-date=1 September 2022|access-date=1 September 2022|author=Yusuf Emir Işık}}</ref>

In his speech at the handover ceremony of the new generation of assault howitzers (MSB Arifiye Campus BMC Plant / Sakarya), President Erdogan said that two new Altay tanks will be manufactured in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.defenceturk.net/mayista-yeni-altay-tanklari-uretim-hattindan-cikacak|title=Mayıs'ta yeni ALTAY tankları üretim hattından çıkacak!|publisher=Defence Turk|date=9 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109213349/https://www.defenceturk.net/mayista-yeni-altay-tanklari-uretim-hattindan-cikacak|archive-date=9 January 2023|access-date=9 January 2022|author=Ahmet Alemdar}}</ref>

On 30 January 2023, BMC signed a supply agreement with SNT Dynamics to purchase the EST15K transmission. The agreement includes a supply contract (approximately €68.926&nbsp;million) to procure 90 transmissions by December 2027 and an option contract (approximately €130,900&nbsp;million) to procure an additional 150 transmissions by December 2030.<ref name="DART SNT Dynamics">{{cite web|url=https://dart.fss.or.kr/dsaf001/main.do?rcpNo=20230130800097|title=Altay전차용 자동변속기 구매공급 계약|publisher=[[Financial Supervisory Service (South Korea)]]|date=30 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230318152507/https://dart.fss.or.kr/dsaf001/main.do?rcpNo=20230130800097|archive-date=18 March 2023|access-date=18 March 2023|author=}}</ref><ref name="Defence Turkey 202302">{{cite web|url=https://www.defenceturkey.com/en/content/est15k-automatic-transmission-order-for-altay-mbt-5416|title=EST15K Automatic Transmission Order for ALTAY MBT|publisher=Defence Turkey|date=February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230318175705/https://www.defenceturkey.com/en/content/est15k-automatic-transmission-order-for-altay-mbt-5416#.ZBX7eXbP2Uk|archive-date=18 March 2023|access-date=18 March 2023|author=}}</ref>

In March 2023, BMC announced it planned to deliver two Altay tanks to the Turkish Armed Forces in April 2023 for field tests expected to last 1.5 to two years, with mass production planned for 2025. Given the number of changes to the project, the company is now referring to the tank as the "Yeni Altay" (New Altay).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-23 |title=Yalçıntaş: "Yeni ALTAY 23 Nisan'da TSK'ya teslim edilecek" |url=https://www.savunmasanayist.com/yalcintas-yeni-altay-23-nisanda-tskya-teslim-edilecek/ |access-date=2023-03-23 |language=tr}}</ref> Mass production officially began on 5 September 2025 with a dedicated factory, which is partially funded by [[Qatar]], officially opened on 28 October 2025.<ref>{{cite web | title=Savunma sanayiinde gurur günü: Altay tankı envantere giriyor | date=28 October 2025 | url=https://www.trthaber.com/haber/gundem/savunma-sanayiinde-gurur-gunu-altay-tanki-envantere-giriyor-924081.html#:~:text=BMC%20taraf%C4%B1ndan%20g%C3%BC%C3%A7%20grubu%20dahil,kazanaca%C4%9F%C4%B1%20T2%20konfig%C3%BCrasyonuyla%20devam%20edecek }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-02|title=Qatar financed 49% of Turkish tank factory|url=https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20210702-qatar-financed-49-of-turkish-tank-factory/|access-date=2021-07-06|website=Middle East Monitor|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In February 2025, Haluk Görgün announced that deliveries of ALTAY tanks in the T1 configuration will begin as of 2025. 3 ALTAY T1 tanks will be delivered in 2025 (5 total delivered). These deliveries are expected to be made in August. 85 tanks in T1 configuration will be delivered, followed by 11 ALTAY tanks in 2026, 41 tanks in 2027 and then 30 tanks. The South Korean power group will be used in the first 40 ALTAY tanks, then the domestic power group will be used and the 1500 horsepower BATU will be used.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-24 |title=ALTAY tankı için teslimat takvimi açıklandı: 250 adet tank geliyor |url=https://www.donanimhaber.com/altay-tanki-teslimat-takvimi-aciklandi-250-adet-tank-geliyor--188174 |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=DonanımHaber |language=tr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Türkiye's Altay tank to enter national inventory in 2025 |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/turkiye/turkiyes-altay-tank-to-enter-national-inventory-in-2025/3492443 |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=www.aa.com.tr}}</ref>

===Design===
The tank benefits both from indigenously developed systems and from technologies of the K2 Black Panther, accorded by an agreement signed with South Korea.<ref name="Design assistance and transfer of Technology 1" /> The main armament of the tank is the 120&nbsp;mm 55 caliber smoothbore gun, which is based on the [[CN08 120 mm gun]] of the K2 Black Panther, was redesigned by [[MKEK]] to remove the autoloader feature in exchange for higher reliability. The [[thermal sleeve]] of the [[gun barrel]]<nowiki> is equipped with a gun stabilizer configured with a static muzzle reference system (SMRS).{{</nowiki>[[Template:Citation needed|Citation needed]]<nowiki>}}</nowiki>

The armor package was modified based on the K2's [[K1 88-Tank#Protection|Korean Special Armor Plate]] (KSAP),<ref name="Samyang Comtech" /> but was redesigned by [[Roketsan]] for higher ballistic protection in the Altay and will include [[CBRN defense]] elements, to protect it from [[chemical warfare|chemical]], [[biological warfare|biological]], [[radiological warfare|radiological]] and [[nuclear warfare|nuclear]] weapons. Also there will be add-on [[reactive armor]]<nowiki>.{{</nowiki>[[Template:Citation needed|Citation needed]]<nowiki>}}</nowiki>

The planned maximum speed of the first batch is set at {{convert|65|kph|mph}}, provided by an {{convert|1500|hp|abbr=on}} engine and the MBTs will be able to function under {{convert|4|m|ft}}<nowiki> of water.{{</nowiki>[[Template:Citation needed|Citation needed]]<nowiki>}} The first mass production tank will be powered by 1,500</nowiki>&nbsp;hp (1,110&nbsp;kW) DV27K engines and EST15K transmissions (6 forward, 3 reverse gears) designed by Hyundai Doosan Infracore (now HD Hyundai Infracore) and SNT Dynamics in South Korea.<ref name="Korean Powerpack 1" /> whereas the latter batches may powered by an BMC Power BATU V12 12 cylinder V type {{convert|1500|hp|abbr=on}} engine.<ref name="Korean Powerpack 1" />

The suspension system adopts [[Hyundai Rotem]]'s non-active in-arm suspension unit (ISU) and includes a track tension system that automatically adjusts the tension of the track.<ref name="BMC ALTAY 1" /><ref name="Defence24 2024-02-07">{{cite web|url=https://defence24.pl/przemysl/k2-w-nowej-odslonie-wywiad|title=K2 w nowej odsłonie [WYWIAD]|publisher=Defence24|date=2 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240702225813/https://defence24.pl/przemysl/k2-w-nowej-odslonie-wywiad|archive-date=2 July 2024|access-date=2 July 2024|author1=Jędrzej Graf}}</ref> For mass production of the suspension system, KUMA, a partner of Hyundai Rotem, is in charge.<ref name="Kum-A">{{cite web|url=https://blog.hyundai-rotem.co.kr/641|title=방산 유압기기를 만드는 현대로템 협력사, 금아하이드파워|publisher=hyundai-rotem|date=30 November 2021|accessdate=23 January 2026|author=}}</ref>

[[ASELSAN]] made electronic systems produced within the scope of Altay Mass Production Project; Fire Control System, Electric Gun and Turret Engagement System, Command Control Communication and Information System, Driver Vision System, Laser Warning System, Remote Controlled Weapon System, Battlefield Recognition and Identification System, Close Range Surveillance System, AKKOR Active Protection System. [[HAVELSAN]] provides training and simulation for maintenance and training.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/ekonomi/yeni-altay-tanki-aselsan-teknolojileriyle-donatildi/2879266 | title=Yeni Altay Tankı, ASELSAN teknolojileriyle donatıldı }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=HAVELSAN develops advanced simulation systems for ALTAY Tank - Defensehere | date=31 October 2025 | url=https://defensehere.com/en/havelsan-develops-advanced-simulation-systems-for-altay-tank/ }}</ref>

While moving at high speeds, to evade ATGM attacks, sudden braking and manoeuvering at severe angles are capabilities that were taken into consideration from early developmental stages. An isolated ammunition compartment (turret bustle) is designed to protect tank crew, alongside fire and explosion suppression systems that are to activate when hit or when the tank is involved in an accident. The tank is to be equipped with sensors for the detection of contaminated air from chemical, biological and nuclear weapons.<ref name="roketsan1">{{cite web|url=http://www.roketsan.com.tr/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/ALTAY.pdf |title=Altay Tank|publisher=Roketsan.com.tr|access-date=2015-02-28|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130228135316/http://www.roketsan.com.tr/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/ALTAY.pdf |archive-date=28 February 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> The tank also has [[Hunter-killer team|hunter-killer engagement capability]].<ref name="military-today"/>

===Prototypes===
[[File:TankAltayT1 (1).jpg|thumb|Otokar Altay T1 baseline prototype on display at IDEF 2019]]
On 29 April 2009, the Subsecretary for Defence Industries of Turkey, Murad Bayar has confirmed at the 9th IDEX International, Defense Industry Fair in Abu Dhabi, that the Turkish tank will be manufactured using only Turkish resources. He added that the research started last week and that he expected to create an authentic tank model specially designed for the needs of the Turkish Armed Forces within 3 years.<ref name="zmn">{{cite web |url=http://www.todayszaman.com/tz-web/detaylar.do?load=detay&link=168240&bolum=105 |title=ATAK helicopter to be airborne before end of 2009 |work=Today's Zaman |access-date=17 April 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090506205044/http://www.todayszaman.com/tz-web/detaylar.do?load=detay&link=168240&bolum=105 |archive-date=6 May 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In September 2010, with approval of the tank subsystems and software by Undersecretariat for Defense Industries, Conceptual Design Phase of the Altay project has been completed. Thus, the project advanced to Detailed Design Phase scheduled to last 30.5 months. The scope of the Detailed Design Phase is to design and integrate interfaces for the selected tank subsystems.<ref name="zmn" />

On 15 October 2010, Otokar signed a contract with MTU and Renk for the supply of power pack. Also, On 15 December 2010, Defence Industry Executive Committee decided to start the development of national power pack.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ssb.gov.tr/WebSite/contentlist.aspx?PageID=921|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101218152322/http://www.ssm.gov.tr/anasayfa/hizli/duyurular/PressReleases/Sayfalar/2010aralikssikbasinaciklamasi.aspx|url-status=dead|title=HATA – SSB|archive-date=18 December 2010|website=www.ssb.gov.tr}}</ref>

On 10 May 2011, Aselsan was contracted by the Undersecretariat for Defense Industries to design and develop two Battlefield Target Identification Device (BTID) prototypes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ssm.gov.tr/home/projects/land/BattleTanks/Sayfalar/mstts.aspx |access-date=21 November 2016 |url-status=dead |title=Battlefield Identification Device |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120331124425/http://www.ssm.gov.tr/home/projects/land/BattleTanks/Sayfalar/mstts.aspx |archive-date=31 March 2012}}</ref>

On 11 May 2011, the mock-up of the Altay was introduced to the public in IDEF2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.worldbulletin.net/?aType=haber&ArticleID=98699 |title=Turkey introduces main battle tank Altay {{pipe}} Politics {{pipe}} Worldbulletin News |publisher=Worldbulletin.net |date=2012-11-15 |access-date=2015-02-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701065135/http://www.worldbulletin.net/?aType=haber&ArticleID=98699 |archive-date=1 July 2015 |url-status=usurped}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5q6L4tgUwqk |title=ALTAY TANK MOCK-UP – IDEF 2011 ISTANBUL |via=YouTube |date=2011-05-13 |access-date=2015-02-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170212053542/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5q6L4tgUwqk |archive-date=12 February 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 18 October 2012, the first Altay was put on trials although lacking side skirts and using a mock-up turret to simulate a real turret.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fbcdn-sphotos-e-a.akamaihd.net/hphotos-ak-snc7/470949_10151461695859196_1602505937_o.jpg|format=JPG|title=Tank photograph|publisher=Fbcdn-sphotos-e-a.akamaihd.net|access-date=2015-02-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150114174427/https://fbcdn-sphotos-e-a.akamaihd.net/hphotos-ak-snc7/470949_10151461695859196_1602505937_o.jpg|archive-date=14 January 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 16 November 2012, two pre-prototype types, named Altay MTR (Mobility Test Rig) and Altay FTR ([[Firepower]] Test Rig),<ref name="Otokar 20150607">{{cite web|url=https://www.otokar.com.tr/tr-tr/urunler/Documents/Janes_OtokarTank100.pdf|title=A century of the tank Mark 1 vs Altay|publisher=[[Otokar]]|date=7 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003102322/https://www.otokar.com.tr/tr-tr/urunler/Documents/Janes_OtokarTank100.pdf|archive-date=3 October 2015|access-date=3 October 2015|author=}}</ref> successfully passed initial acceptance tests, paving the way for serial production 2 years earlier than expected, with two more prototypes to be built by 2013 or 2014.<ref name="Defence Turkey 201211">{{cite web|url=https://www.defenceturkey.com/en/content/the-first-prototypes-of-altay-turkish-national-main-battle-tank-demonstrated-their-mobility-842|title=The First Prototypes of Altay Turkish National Main Battle Tank Demonstrated their Mobility|publisher=Defence Turkey|date=November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706135936/https://www.defenceturkey.com/en/content/the-first-prototypes-of-altay-turkish-national-main-battle-tank-demonstrated-their-mobility-842|archive-date=6 July 2022|access-date=6 July 2022|author=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkey-to-reveal-local-tank-ahead-of-deadline.aspx?pageID=238&nID=34770&NewsCatID=344 |title=Turkey to reveal local tank ahead of deadline – ECONOMICS |date=15 November 2012 |publisher=Hurriyetdailynews.com |access-date=2015-02-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121117104158/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkey-to-reveal-local-tank-ahead-of-deadline.aspx?pageID=238&nID=34770&NewsCatID=344 |archive-date=17 November 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://en.trend.az/regions/met/turkey/2088584.html |title=Altay tank project moves Turkey up a league in defense |publisher=En.trend.az |date=2012-11-16 |access-date=2015-02-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121119082136/http://en.trend.az/regions/met/turkey/2088584.html |archive-date=19 November 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 7 November 2016, MTR, FTR, PV1 and PV2 (Pilot Vehicle) prototypes made by Otokar were delivered to the [[Turkish Land Forces]], and their acceptance tests were expected to finish in the last quarter of 2016 or early 2017.<ref name="Otokar 20150607" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.c4defence.com/Gundem/karaaslan-uc-prototipin-testleri-2017de-tamamlanirsa-altay-tanki-2018de-uretilir/2902/1 |title=Karaaslan: üç prototipin testleri 2017'de tamamlanırsa Altay Tankı 2018'de üretilir |publisher=c4defence.com |date=2016-11-07 |access-date=2016-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121232907/http://www.c4defence.com/Gundem/karaaslan-uc-prototipin-testleri-2017de-tamamlanirsa-altay-tanki-2018de-uretilir/2902/1 |archive-date=21 November 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref> Another prototype variant called Altay AHT (Asimetrik Harp Tankı - "urban operations tank") was showcased by Otokar at the IDEF'17 defense and aerospace show in Istanbul on May 9–12. The tank is equipped with a directional dozer blade.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.defensenews.com/land/2017/05/19/turkish-company-otokar-reveals-urban-operation-tank/| title=Otokar Unveiled Altay-AHT, Urban Operations Tank| date=19 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.defensenews.com/land/2017/05/19/turkish-company-otokar-reveals-urban-operation-tank/| title=Turkish company Otokar reveals 'urban operation tank'| date=19 May 2017}}</ref>

In May 2019, the new developer BMC unveiled Altay's revised baseline serial production model, named T1, at the IDEF Defense Exhibition.{{citation needed|date=November 2025}} On 23 April 2023, 2 T1 variant Altays were delivered to TAF for further evaluation and testing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://shiftdelete.net/yeni-altay-tanki-hakkinda-tum-merak-edilenler|title=Yeni Altay tankı hakkında tüm merak edilenler! - ShiftDelete.Net|date=23 March 2023 |access-date=11 February 2024}}</ref>

===Contractors and subcontractors===
Subsequently, in accordance with the later Defense Industries Executive Committee ruling, approximately 200 subcontractors were selected.<ref name="SSB 1"/> Main ones are as follows:
* Design and development: [[Otokar]]<ref name="roketsan1"/>
* Design assistance and technology transfer: [[Hyundai Rotem]]<ref name="Design assistance and transfer of Technology 1" />
* Main contractor, manufacturer: [[BMC Otomotiv|BMC]] (replaced Otokar)<ref name="SSB 1"/>
* Main [[smoothbore]] gun subcontractor: state owned [[MKEK]]<ref name="SSB 1"/>
* Main smoothbore gun technology transfer: [[Hyundai WIA]]<ref name="Design assistance and transfer of Technology 1" />
* [[Rolled homogeneous armour|Rolled homogeneous armor]] (MIL-12560H): [[POSCO]]<ref name="POSCO NEWSROOM 2020-07-23">{{cite web|url=https://newsroom.posco.com/kr/%ED%8F%AC%EC%8A%A4%EC%BD%94%EC%97%90%EB%8F%84-bts%EA%B0%80-%EC%9E%88%EB%8B%A4/|title=포스코에도 BTS가 있다|publisher=[[POSCO]]|date=23 July 2025|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210717091251/https://newsroom.posco.com/kr/%ED%8F%AC%EC%8A%A4%EC%BD%94%EC%97%90%EB%8F%84-bts%EA%B0%80-%EC%9E%88%EB%8B%A4/|archivedate=17 July 2021|accessdate=17 July 2021|author1=}}</ref>
* [[Vehicle armour|Armor]] package subcontractor: [[Roketsan]]<ref name="roketsan1"/>
* Armor package technology transfer and supply of [[Ballistic plate#Ceramic|ceramic ballistic plate]]s: [[Samyang Comtech]]<ref name="Design assistance and transfer of Technology 1" /><ref name="Samyang Comtech History" />
* Armor package design assistance: [[Poongsan Corporation]]<ref name="Design assistance and transfer of Technology 1" />
* [[Continuous track]] development and subcontractor: [[LS Mtron]]<ref name="LS Mtron Defense">{{cite web|url=https://www.lstrackshoe.com/upload/applications/mrftod2tclamilmt04f0.pdf|title=LS DEFENSE EQUIPMENT|publisher=[[LS Mtron]]|date=|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251214143326/https://www.lstrackshoe.com/upload/applications/mrftod2tclamilmt04f0.pdf|archivedate=14 December 2025|accessdate=14 December 2025|author1=}}</ref><ref name="LS Mtron History">{{cite web|url=https://www.lstrackshoe.com/en/defense/history|title=History|publisher=[[LS Mtron]]|date=2025|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250425114153/https://www.lstrackshoe.com/en/defense/history|archivedate=25 April 2025|accessdate=25 April 2025|author1=}}</ref>
* [[Hydropneumatic suspension|Hydropneumatic suspension system]] subcontractor: Hyundai Rotem<ref name="Defence24 2024-02-07" />
* [[Powerpack (drivetrain)|Powerpack]] subcontractor (initial, canceled): [[MTU Friedrichshafen|MTU]] Engine<ref name="SSB 1"/> & [[Renk]] Transmission<ref name="SSB 1"/>
* Powerpack subcontractor (first batch): [[HD Hyundai Infracore]] (engine)<ref name="Korean Powerpack 1" /> and [[SNT Dynamics]] (transmission)<ref name="Korean Powerpack 1" />
* Powerpack subcontractor (second batch): [[BMC Otomotiv|BMC]] Power<ref name="SSB 1"/>
* Sub-systems subcontractor: [[Aselsan]] and [[HAVELSAN]]<ref name="SSB 1"/>

==Variants==
*'''Altay T0''' – baseline prototype variant.<ref name="SSB 1"/>
*'''Altay T1''' - serial production variant with Korean powerpack<ref name="nationalfeb2025">{{cite web | url=https://nationalinterest.org/blog/buzz/turkey-is-building-a-domestic-tank-arsenal| title=Turkey Is Building A Domestic Tank Arsenal| publisher=[[The National Interest]]| author= Peter Suciu| date=27 February 2025 }}</ref>
*'''Altay T2''' – improved serial production variant with Turkish powerpack.<ref name="nationalfeb2025"/>
*'''Altay T3''' – planned variant with unmanned turret.<ref name="nationalfeb2025"/>
* Engineering: Bridge Layer, Mine Clearing and Recovery Vehicle variants are planned.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.savunmasanayist.com/altay-tanki-sasesinden-uc-farkli-arac-gelistiriliyor/ | title=ALTAY tankı şasesinden üç farklı araç geliştiriliyor | date=17 October 2023 }}</ref>

==Foreign interest==
* {{AZE}} - At [[International Defence Industry Fair|IDEF-2013]], the [[Azerbaijan Army]] expressed interest in Altay.<ref>{{cite web | title=Azərbaycan Türkiyədən "Altay" tankları ALACAQ | url=https://modern.az/az/news/531237/ }}</ref>
* {{COL}} - According to reports, a military envoy from Colombia was present at the 2010 press meeting hosted by the Undersecreteriat for Defense Industries of the Republic of Turkey to obtain more information about the tank.<ref name="TRdefenceColombia"/>
* {{IDN}} - In October 2025, Indonesian media reported that the [[Indonesian Army]] was planning to acquire 100 units of the Altay main battle tank from Turkey.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://teknologi.bisnis.com/read/20251029/84/1924206/prabowo-dikabarkan-boyong-100-unit-tank-mbt-altay-buatan-turki-ini-spesifikasinya |title=Prabowo Dikabarkan Boyong 100 Unit Tank MBT Altay Buatan Turki, Ini Spesifikasinya |date=29 October 2025 |website=Bisnis.com |language=id}}</ref>
* {{SAU}} - In April 2013, officials of the [[Saudi Arabian Army]] reportedly became interested in Altay.<ref name="defensenews.com">{{cite news|title=Turkish Tank Sees Pakistani, Saudi Interest|url=http://www.defensenews.com/story/defense/land/vehicles/2016/01/15/turkish-tank-sees-pakistani-saudi-interest/78844970/|date=19 June 2016}}</ref> Also in 2025, it is reported that Turkey has been aiming to secure a $6 billion defense deal with Saudi Arabia which includes Altays.<ref>{{cite web | title=Turkey seeks $6 billion arms deal with Saudi Arabia: Report | date=27 January 2025 | url=https://www.duvarenglish.com/turkey-seeks-6-billion-arms-deal-with-saudi-arabia-report-news-65596#:~:text=Duvar%20English,likely%20to%20discuss%20the%20agreement }}</ref>
* {{OMN}} - Otokar was invited to a bid for 77 Altays for a tender in Oman in August 2013.<ref>{{cite web | title=Report: Oman May Acquire German Leopard Tanks | date=13 November 2015 | url=https://www.defensenews.com/land/2015/11/13/report-oman-may-acquire-german-leopard-tanks/ }}</ref>
* {{PAK}} - Pakistan has also shown interest in procuring the Altay for their armed forces in 2016.<ref name="defensenews.com"/>
* {{QAT}} - In March 2019, a senior Turkish politician stated an order for total 100 tanks was placed by Qatar.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Herschelman |first1=Kerry |title=Qatar planning to buy Altay tanks |url=https://www.janes.com/article/87328/qatar-planning-to-buy-altay-tanks |website=Jane's 360 |access-date=19 March 2019 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190319214419/https://www.janes.com/article/87328/qatar-planning-to-buy-altay-tanks |archive-date=19 March 2019 |location=Washington, DC |date=19 March 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>
